headlineOutcome: Stephanie Dailey saved over $20,000 in taxes in her first year
summary: Stephanie and her husband are software engineers with five kids and over $300,000 in W-2 income, plus contract work from the consulting business they run. In her first year in the Legacy Wealth Blueprint she opened separate business bank accounts, started keeping real books, captured $27,000 in startup costs, deducted over $60,000 of bridge loan mortgage interest and put her kids on payroll through Gusto. She expects $40,000 to $50,000 over the following twelve months, and says the plan to pay off the house moved from about ten years to seven or eight.
keyQuotes: financially, we're high income on paper, but we also have real expenses, multiple income streams, and just a lot of moving pieces
it might have otherwise taken me years to get where we got in six months
we were just really blown away by how quickly it paid off
I would say, don't hesitate.

headlineOutcome: Albert put his net worth growth at 25% and cut his home insurance in half
summary: Albert is an ER physician in California who finished residency in 2021 with about $5,000 in a Roth and a combined tax bracket he puts at almost 50%. In the Legacy Wealth Blueprint he started tax loss harvesting, changed how he uses his HSA, opened a backdoor Roth IRA, took his portfolio off professional management and formed the entity for a new telemedicine clinic. He says his self-managed 401(k) is up about 19% year to date and his Roth about 40%.
keyQuotes: Before Legacy Wealth Blueprint, I would say the amount of financial knowledge I had was super slim.
Since I live in California, my tax bracket is almost 50%, including federal and state.
I had no idea about tax loss harvesting.
I would say the information you provide is pretty priceless.

headlineOutcome: Abigail calculated just under $100,000 in first-year ROI
summary: Abigail left oil and gas in the summer of 2023 and runs the numbers for her own family and her parents. She finished the Legacy Wealth Blueprint modules inside the first month, rebuilt the entity and estate work she had set up badly eight years earlier, took a weekly coaching call with her coach Brandon, recategorized every transaction as business or not business, and went under contract on her first property. The just under $100,000 is her own calculation, run twice.
keyQuotes: I have really more of the attitude that I really can't let another dollar go by that's not working for me.
a high yield savings account, the 4% at some point 5%, wasn't going to get me to freedom. That was just keeping me from drowning
I'm coming in at just under a hundred thousand dollars ROI for just this year.
don't be afraid to be the person in the room who knows the least

headlineOutcome: Shawn came for the tax knowledge his CPAs were not giving him
summary: Shawn is a business owner who already held Airbnbs, rentals, crypto and stocks. What he did not have was the tax side, and he says he was struggling to get useful help from CPAs. This interview runs about a minute and carries no dollar figures, because he is at the start of his plan rather than the end of it.
keyQuotes: The bigger picture was getting the knowledge from you, the professional, in the taxes, because I'm struggling right now with CPAs.
I had a clear direction of where I needed to go
Who knows? It could be tremendous.
If I truly play the game with you and I'm a good student and I follow the steps, oh yeah, for me, this is life-changing for sure.

headlineOutcome: Rob clears more than $10,000 a month from two Airbnb properties in Louisville and St. Simons Island
summary: Rob was a sales professional with two young kids when he chose the arbitrage model over buying so he would not tie up capital in down payments. He runs two properties, one in Louisville, Kentucky and one on St. Simons Island, Georgia, for over $10,000 a month in combined profit. Louisville costs him $3,600 a month all in and peaked above $5,000 profit in Derby month; the St. Simons house sleeps 15 with a pool and hot tub. After systems were in place he reports about two hours of work a week.
keyQuotes: I wanted to get into real estate but the idea of okay we gotta get through the process of putting a down payment down and then that ties up your capital versus okay well what if you just do the arbitrage model where you can actually scale a lot quicker.

It's in my best interest to maintain your place and if not even make it better than where I found it because if I can't book this you don't get paid, I don't get paid, nobody wins. And for almost everybody I've talked to they're like yeah this is a no-brainer.

Get as many nos as you can as quickly as possible. In my sales days that's what it was—the quicker you start to realize okay where am I hitting that stopping point, cool now I'm gonna know that for the next call going in.
Don't sit on the sidelines guys. If you fail you fail, but you don't get anywhere by sitting on the sidelines.

headlineOutcome: Gary makes $35,000 a month from seven Austin properties, three years in
summary: Gary was a marketing executive at eBay and Chegg before building an Airbnb business in Austin, Texas. He runs seven properties with an eighth in progress, targets $10,000 gross and $5,000 to $6,000 net per property, and holds a 50% margin across the portfolio. He picks markets he would live in himself, treats pools and large guest capacity as the filter that removes competitors, and avoids month-long stays because discounted long guests demand repairs short guests never mention.
keyQuotes: One of my number one rules about Airbnb property management or investing is really trying to go into a place where I enjoy living at. Austin is one of those places I could totally see myself moving to.

If I take away a pool, if I take away the jacuzzi, if I take away the 15 people capacity to only 10 people, now the filter basically puts me in competition with a lot more properties. So the property that has all these amenities becomes one of the few houses that has it.

When I start lowering the prices, what I actually see is that the quality of the guest starts deteriorating. People that book in advance are higher quality because they're not procrastinators—they're really thinking about booking everything.
There's many different ways to attack this problem or attack this industry. You really want to just pick the brains of people that are already doing it and share knowledge.

headlineOutcome: Michael locked up two Space Coast deals in one week and projects $12,000 a month
summary: Michael is a serial entrepreneur who sold five companies before moving into Airbnb arbitrage on the Space Coast of Florida. He locked up two deals in one week, went from joining the program to a live listing in six weeks, and took his first booking five minutes after the listing went live. He reports a 60% close rate on landlord pitches, built around a service pitch aimed at travelling nurses and first responders, and imputes an 8% mortgage cost even on the property he owns outright.
keyQuotes: In five minutes it got listed and that's it. We're ocean view, two minute walk to the beach, rocket launches behind you. It literally got sucked up in seconds.

I see a lot of people in the group just giving up and saying 'oh I called three or four and they turned me down.' Okay there's 20 others. Why aren't you making 20 calls? I would hunt the best areas, circle them, and just blast them.

A lot of entrepreneurs and Airbnb people tend to leave that out. They say 'oh I own it so I don't pay a mortgage.' Yeah but you don't realize because you're not paying a mortgage that money should be making you some kind of money.

How much would I ever have to pay or learn or go through trial and error to get to that point? For me to do what you gave me for your nominal amount would have cost me hundreds of thousands of dollars in headaches and mistakes.

headlineOutcome: Brian O'Leary makes $1,500 to $2,000 a month from one Iowa property, 30 days from joining to signed lease
summary: Brian works full time in IT and added an Airbnb arbitrage unit in Iowa rather than buying another property. The four-bedroom historic home sleeps ten, went live in February and was cash flow positive by March at $1,500 to $2,000 a month after expenses. He landed the lease by borrowing the credibility of an existing operator team and their Superhost listings, and now runs it on one to two hours a week with automation.
keyQuotes: I wanted to expand and instead of expanding into purchasing more properties, I decided to check out this arbitrage model. I'm using it to bring in more cash, and then properties that make sense, I'll see if there's an opportunity to switch from renting to owning.

That's where just having a group of people behind me was really helpful. I was able to tell her, 'Yes, while I am new to this, I am part of a team that has done this for dozens of homes and they are Superhosts. Here's a link to a few of those you can check them out. The level of quality photos and reviews you're seeing on these listings - that's what I'm going to bring to your property.'
We started in this market because I wanted to start somewhat close to home. I really wanted to be there, to stage it, to see what things were looking like from beginning to end.

We've had guests that asked if there was a crib or a child gate and we just said yes, went out and bought it. This is a four bedroom house catered to families, so it's going to be good to have those things and be able to say yes to future guests.

headlineOutcome: Grayson Nichols hit 75% occupancy and $3,500 a month by his third month near Austin
summary: Grayson is a remote IT worker who took six months to work through the program before going live in July 2023 with one property near Austin, Texas. Profit went from $1,000 in September to $3,500 in October at 75% occupancy, with most bookings coming from VRBO and a booking horizon stretching six months out. He negotiated a $2,300 security deposit into lawn and property improvements instead of a cash hold, and won the lease by meeting the owner in person.
keyQuotes: I work remotely. I do IT, so it's very easy to do from my laptop wherever I am. It also gave me a lot of time to do the modules whenever I had just some downtime.
October is currently our busiest month. We've got about 75% of this month booked out. It's been great.

One of the things you teach in your course is trying to use that security deposit as just money that you can reinvest into the house. I was actually able to get the landlord to agree to let me use that $2,300 to revamp the lawn.
I think what really helped is I was willing to actually meet her here and kind of just walk through everything. She was able to see that I was a real person.

headlineOutcome: Marchia and Cash took one Atlanta property from $2,400 in February to $6,000 in April
summary: Brothers Marchia, 27, and Cash, 23, built an Airbnb arbitrage business in downtown Atlanta, one of the most crowded markets in the country. Their first property went from $2,400 in February to $4,950 in March and over $6,000 in April with a week still open, against $3,200 a month in rent, and AirDNA puts the annual run rate at $70,000 to $75,000. They differentiate by studying the reviews of the top-rated Atlanta listings and building a themed property rather than another nice house.
keyQuotes: We know that it's a long road and it's a hard road that not many people take. And we know that you will reap the benefits as long as you keep your nose to the grindstone and work hard day in and day out.
We know there's always going to be travelers in Atlanta, especially downtown Atlanta. There's just people coming in. So it's about—are you able to stand out within that saturated space?

I go look at all the ones in Atlanta that have 55 star reviews and that's all they got, or 105 star reviews with a 5.0. And then I go read the reviews to see what are all the things that they're doing right.
So we're trying to differentiate ourselves by bringing the theme to it—something a little more fun than just a nice house.

headlineOutcome: Tom booked $25,000 in his first two weeks live on the Chesapeake Bay
summary: Tom was a Capital One executive with a software engineering background and no rental experience when he launched his first Airbnb on the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland. In the first two weeks live he booked $25,000 through August and into September, and he now runs $5,000 to $6,000 a month in cash flow on 20 to 30 minutes a day. He built a three-person cleaning team for redundancy and chose a beach property he initially doubted, until his grandchildren showed him what guests would come for.
keyQuotes: These corporate gigs just suck the life out of you. I had to put this all on pause for a few months because we had a bunch of end of year activities that consumes everybody.
Don't look at it like this horrible situation, this risky thing. Look at it like an adventure and keep your attitude kind of positive.
To be honest with you, when I first saw it I was kind of like, 'I don't know, that's a beautiful piece of property but I'm not sure people are going to want to go here.'
My grandkids came down, they played on that beach all day and I'm like, 'That's a key, that is a key right there.'

headlineOutcome: Kiana left a ten year finance career and makes $3,200 a month from two Scottsdale properties
summary: Kiana spent more than a decade in finance and six months researching short-term rental rules across the country before acting. She now runs two properties ten minutes apart in Scottsdale, Arizona for $3,200 a month in combined cash flow, quit her job three months after joining, and has cut weekly management from ten hours to four. Her first property hit its conservative $2,500 a month benchmark, and when Airbnb demand softened she converted it to a one-year tenancy at the same number.
keyQuotes: I've always believed in Financial Freedom. I also worked in finance for over a decade so I kind of have a little knowledge in that. I started researching this for like the last six months.
What do I have to lose and everything to gain? The overhead cost is not that much and the return is so high.

I had probably spent six months kind of just going around the whole entire United States kind of researching understanding short-term laws. I think that is kind of the higher risk on the sides of things so that was my biggest challenge.
We did the Airbnb for the first two months and then we actually were able to find a one-year tenant and so it still hit the same conservative Benchmark.

headlineOutcome: Dustin Cotton makes $6,000 a month from two Texas properties, four weeks from joining to first lease
summary: Dustin came from corporate sales with no rental experience and runs two lakefront properties in Texas for about $6,000 a month in cash flow. He spent three weeks on research without making a call, found his first markets were hostile or crowded, then lined up five interested landlords across one weekend of eight to ten hour calling days. The first property took $15,000 to start against $2,500 a month rent on a three-year lease, and grosses $6,000 to $7,500 a month where the previous operator had managed $1,000.
keyQuotes: The detail of your content and the sincerity that you put towards your program - I was like, this is it, let's go.
I spent three weeks doing that without making a phone call. I started calling into these markets and I realized the particular areas in those markets I was calling into - they were not friendly.
Saturday and Sunday I spent maybe eight to ten hours both days in combination calling and I lined up five properties that landlords were like, let's go.

Some of the best opportunities are the ones that on whatever they're marketing the property have bad pictures. You've got to go to Google Earth and see where it's actually at, have a vision for it, because bad pictures is almost like a diamond in the rough.

headlineOutcome: Lindsay and her husband booked $17,500 in their first week live in the North Carolina mountains
summary: Lindsay and her husband moved from nonprofit and 9-to-5 work into Airbnb arbitrage in the Western North Carolina mountains, thirty minutes outside Asheville. They went from first landlord contact to a signed contract in 21 days and secured the property on their fourth call. Fourteen days after going live on September 7 they had $17,500 booked across 14 reservations through New Year's Eve, with peak cash flow of $2,500 to $3,000 a month and about three hours of work a week.
keyQuotes: We just got married a year and a half ago so this was a new adventure even as a married couple. Finances can be a sticking point for couples, and it's just neat that we both hopped in on this together.
We just knew we wanted to get on the market as soon as we could because the fall is peak season up here with the Western North Carolina mountains. So we were pressing them a little bit.
We saw that on the AirDNA it showed that less than 20% of that area had the hot tub so we wanted to make sure we did that just to stand out.
We named it something that people could remember so they'll come back to and we'll have repeat guests.

headlineOutcome: Hampton booked $20,000 in his first month on his parents' lakefront home
summary: Hampton is a process engineer who started with his parents' lakefront property, showing them a projection of what the weekends they were not using could earn. The listing booked $20,000 within weeks and over $30,000 across four months. He has since added a West Virginia property returning 25 to 30% cash on cash, has a seven-bedroom lodge in progress, and manages the portfolio in about an hour a day using a local team he can message for on-site issues.
keyQuotes: I actually took some of the tools that you kind of provided with us that were like a lot so far as breaking down what to expect and stuff and I took that and showed them. I said look this is what it's a great property, we love being up there. But here's what you could make if we rented it on some of the weekends we're not there.
Using that information we knew what we could do, we knew what we could use that to back into what we wanted to put into the little house to start with to get it up and running.

Having a good team or having a good list of people to call in that general area that can help out and go address these issues, and all I have to do is send a message to somebody be like hey can you do you mind stepping over here I need you to check this out.
Been extremely nervous about it but sometimes you just got to take a leap of faith and take the risk and it's definitely panning out.

headlineOutcome: Andrew Wolf averages $1,500 a month from a Tulum Airbnb he runs remotely from the United States
summary: Andrew came from hotel management and runs a single arbitrage property in Tulum, Mexico entirely from the United States. Year one averaged about $1,500 a month across seasons, with nightly rates swinging from $400 in high season to $100 in the summer, and he projects $2,500 a month in year two once the new airport opens. He spends about five hours a week on it and says the program's landlord approach and numbers work were what made an international deal executable.
keyQuotes: I was very interested in the concept but I did not have at that time a way to really execute it. There were a lot of questions I had. After going through the program, everything started to click as far as how to approach landlords and putting all the pieces together.
Going through the modules of the program helped a lot on the negotiation stage. I knew what I needed for numbers to get out what I wanted to make it worth my time to even put any money down.

Air DNA was helpful although it's not as complete in some of those markets as it would be here in the US. But that was a big tool that helped me narrow down whether it was a profitable market to access.
Finding the right partners really gave me confidence. They were focused on Airbnb arbitrage so they understood the concept and were trying to tailor their program to that.

headlineOutcome: Christopher Bamford makes $1,700 a month in Louisiana after 50 to 70 landlord calls
summary: Christopher started out buying at garage sales to run an eBay business and could never find a way into real estate with the capital normally required. He made 50 to 70 landlord calls and lost several deals where the numbers did not work before signing a three-year lease on a Louisiana property that now returns over $1,700 a month. He rehearsed the landlord script with his father for an hour and a half, and differentiates on a pool, which only about 6% of local listings have, plus a boho theme.
keyQuotes: I've always kind of been in the entrepreneur spirit. I started with like 70 bucks going to garage sales and started an eBay business. I could really never find my way into real estate with the capital that you have to have and just not knowing and not necessarily having guidance on it.

I called my father and I started practicing with him. I was like hey look you're going to be a landlord, I'm gonna come in—and I probably sat on the phone with him for probably about an hour and a half and just went over the script, went over the script. Just repetition is what it is because it starts to become memory, you just start to be able to spit it out.
You start getting excited and then the numbers just don't work and you gotta take your feelings out of it because that's what it comes down to—it comes down to the numbers and this is a business.

He kind of told me a story where we kind of connected. I was like hey this is my first investment property and he was like a guy took a chance on me seven years ago and now I have 26 properties. If the numbers work and everything's legit on your end, I would love to get you into investing.

headlineOutcome: Kirk hit 87% occupancy and $5,500 in March from one California property while nursing full time
summary: Kirk is a full-time nurse in California who had never started a business before. He projected $2,000 a month conservatively and the property has run ahead of that, at $5,500 in March on 87% occupancy and over $4,400 in April on 70%. He dislikes phone calls, so he pitched owners and property managers face to face at the properties instead, and he set the listing apart from the neutral farmhouse look common in his area by using colour.
keyQuotes: My ultimate goal is to spend more time with my family. I want the time and freedom to actually be here for them, see them grow up. That's why I'm doing this.

Initially I don't like talking on the phone. I try to prevent that as much as possible. But this really got my feet wet. In the beginning a lot of people were saying no, but I saw that as more of an incentive.
Instead of actually making the phone call, I would go see the property, talk to the owners, talk to the property manager, and pitch them in front of me.
Most of the people in my area have just the neutral color farmhouse type. So I tried to set us apart by putting a little bit more color, things to make it pop.

headlineOutcome: Sunny makes $2,000 to $5,000 a month from one Houston townhouse near the Texas Medical Center
summary: Sunny is a respiratory therapist who runs a five-bedroom, four-storey townhouse six minutes from the Texas Medical Center in Houston. He found Preston Seo through Instagram reels, spent four months from Thanksgiving to a March launch, and now holds a baseline above $2,000 a month with a peak of $5,216 during a Taylor Swift concert month. His thesis is the families and out-of-state visitors who need space and privacy near the medical center for extended stays rather than a hotel room.
keyQuotes: I was on Instagram, I was on YouTube. I came across your IG profile and I watched your reels and I just got hooked on. And I signed up for your class and that's how I dive into it.

As I'm working I'm like, you know, there are families who are visiting the medical center who want to stay with the children or the relatives for extended periods of time or just some visitors from out of state coming in.
If there's a property around here, instead of just going to a hotel you can book a house that has a sense of privacy and enough space for enough visitors.

That's one of the views that my guests told me, it feels home away from home. And I feel like that's what I want for my properties to feel like, it's not just like a place that I just bought so I can make money off of it, it's also my home that I'm willing to share.
